algorithm: Otherwise, construct the graph from n and edges
Use Dijkstra's algorithm (for unweighted graphs, this is equivalent to BFS) to compute shortest path length from source to target
If no path exists, raise ValueError
constraints: edges must be distinct and satisfy 0<=u<v<n
source and target must be valid vertices (0<=vertex<n)
The graph is simple undirected unweighted
The algorithm must use BFS for unweighted graphs (Dijkstra's algorithm for weighted, but here weight=1)
edge_cases: n=1: single vertex with no edges
No path exists between source and target: raise ValueError
Graph has isolated vertices (vertices with no edges)
inputs: n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs with 0<=u<v<n; source: string (valid vertex); target: string (valid vertex)
output: integer shortest-path length from source to target (0 if source==target), or raise ValueError if no path exists
purpose: Compute the shortest path length between two vertices in a simple undirected unweighted graph
